description: A fail-closed external audit ledger for Cortexel coverage of the official NEST Simulator v3.10 example corpus. V1 closes only the pinned source, alias, selector, canonical-entrypoint, runner-target-profile, and checked-in-asset denominator. It deliberately admits no visual-output, mapping, adapter, renderer, upstream-execution, or scientific-certification rows. This mutable audit evidence remains outside the normative package contract and establishes no visualization coverage.

limitations: The inventory binds the pinned commit's Git SHA-1 object identities and source roles; its outer SHA-256 digest binds those identifiers, not independently rehashed source-blob bytes. It does not classify plotting callsites or the semantics of any source body.
A documentation reference is selector evidence, not a process invocation; it never contributes to the runner-target-profile count.

A runner target profile records one member of the canonical sorted target set, its Python argv, working directory, and runner-owned environment fields. It neither preserves the runner's filesystem-dependent execution order nor models the surrounding time, shell, redirection, and logging wrapper; it is a definition rather than an execution receipt and does not close inherited ambient dependencies.
A checked-in PNG, GIF, or SVG is a source-tree asset; its presence does not establish that an example emits, consumes, or semantically matches that asset.
Source closure transfers no evidence to visual-output inventory, stable mapping, packaged implementation, rendering, upstream execution, or scientific certification.
sourceInventory.notes: The canonical artifact was generated from a temporary Git repository after fetching the exact commit, materializing only the bounded selector and alias blobs needed for this inventory, removing every configured remote, and verifying repository-local object authority before reading the inventory. No upstream Python code was imported or executed. The artifact contains 112 Python paths (109 regular bodies and 3 aliases), 98 canonical entrypoint bodies, 92 executable runner target definitions, and 12 checked-in visual assets.

evidenceAxes.notes: The exact pinned source artifact closes paths, aliases, documentation and default-runner selectors, canonical entrypoints, executable runner target definitions, and checked-in visual assets for its declared scope.
No figure, panel, overlay, table, animation, interactive surface, emitted artifact, stdout report, or reviewed no-output result has been admitted.
No official-example output has been assigned a stable Cortexel mapping or an explicit infeasibility result.
The existence of package adapters is not projected onto any official example until a visual output and its source profile have been assessed.
No stable renderer has been compared with an inventoried official-example visual output.
No bounded execution receipt exists for an official target under the pinned NEST authority.
No pinned output has an independent source-to-adapter-to-renderer comparison receipt or scientific oracle.

knownUnsupportedInterfaces.notes: Stable contracts describe connection mappings, but the package ships no executable FigureRequestV1 GetConnections adapter.
Stable contracts describe analog mappings, but the package ships no executable FigureRequestV1 voltmeter or multimeter adapter.
Stable contracts describe position mappings, but the package ships no executable FigureRequestV1 GetPosition adapter.
Neither the TypeScript package nor the independent Python reader starts or introspects a live PyNEST simulation.
ASCII, screen, MPI, and SIONlib recorder outputs are outside the one packaged plain-data adapter profile.
The packaged spike-recorder adapter rejects time_in_steps true because the current stable request does not preserve NEST's step-plus-offset clock authority.

summary.notes: The source denominator is closed, but every visualization-evidence count remains zero. This ledger establishes no Cortexel coverage of official NEST examples.
